implemented_requirements.evidence: DIFFICULTIES = {"Beginner": (9, 9, 10), "Intermediate": (16, 16, 40), "Expert": (16, 30, 99)} in game.py and the top‑bar creates a button for each name in ui.py.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: In ui.py, each button is created with command=lambda r=r, c=c: self.on_left_click(r, c) which calls game.reveal(r, c).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGame.place_mines computes cell.adjacent; ui.update_display shows b.config(text=str(cell.adjacent) if cell.adjacent else "") for revealed non‑mine cells.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Uncovering a mine ends the game with a loss
implemented_requirements.evidence: In MinesweeperGame.reveal, if cell.mine: cell.revealed = True; self.game_over = True. ui.end_game shows a "Boom!" message when game_over and not won.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board display updates after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: ui.update_display is called after every left or right click, refreshing labels, colors and relief of all buttons.
ui.on_right_click calls game.toggle_flag(r, c); toggle_flag flips cell.flagged when not revealed.
When cell.flagged, ui.update_display configures the button with text="F", bg="yellow", fg="red", relief="raised".

judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional classic Minesweeper game with three difficulty levels, click‑to‑reveal, automatic number calculation, loss on mine, win detection, a flagging system, and clear visual cues for flagged cells. The Tkinter UI updates the board after each action, and the overall structure is runnable. No critical defects are evident, so the submission meets the benchmark requirements.
